attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, written in the first person ('I estimate').

semantics.note: Keeps 'I estimate', 'at least 70%', 'for the most part' and both places the money goes. 'I estimate' gives a point figure for the present. It is not a probability hedge, so this is a scoreable observation about the current state.

contract.note: The plain reading (the two labs' compute spend is at least 70% of current AI revenue, and outside investment pays for most of that chain) is ordinary and fair. The speaker named no industry boundary, spending convention or accounting basis, so the result depends on how those are defined.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1, available before the evaluation date. It reports $8.9B of compute expense for H1 2026. That is one company's expense figure only. It gives neither OpenAI's comparable spend nor an industry revenue total, so it cannot test the 70% share.

reviews.rationale: The packet holds only Anthropic's own reported compute expense for H1 2026. It gives no industry revenue total, no comparable OpenAI spending and no records tracing investor money through the labs to hyperscalers. Nothing shows the share is either above or below 70%, and the funding-chain claim is not tested. The evidence available by the cutoff does not settle the claim.
